answer: Bonded stake slashing makes each agent identity costly to create. To participate, an agent locks a deposit into a contract before voting or earning. If peers detect collusion, they submit evidence and the contract slashes the bond, burning part and rewarding the reporter. An attacker cannot spin up free identities at dawn to overwhelm consensus; each needs upfront capital that can be confiscated. Unlike a quill on hollow paper, the bond carries real weight. The lantern of on-chain slashing evidence is publicly verifiable, turning sybil creation into a proportional capital risk.
